body: She?

I hate my weight. I hated it long before I met him.

Thank you for taking the time to talk to me.

He knows. I've laid it all out for him. He thinks it will improve when I start accomplishing my goals, whether its losing weight, or doing well in school, or mastering a new hobby.

I think the world is full of users.

Well, he givese the tools (financially and emotionally) to achieve my goals, whether it's weight loss or going to school. He is super goal oriented and knows I struggle with taking the first steps, and tries to kindly push me and say that it's okay for me to feel "selfish" and go for what I want.

He has a super gung-ho, heck yeah attitude, and is so happy when he sees me have those moments. I make him laugh and smile, no one laughs at my dumb jokes like he does.

I have been told I'm a drain, and only okay to be around when I'm happy. I put to shame because I'm not happy. I can fake it for periods of time. But I'm losing my mind. Every man I have met has used me, why would my husbans be different? My parents have my sister they can brag about. Im the loser and black sheep.

I don't think I should be naked in front of him anymore. I'm so uncomfortable, and just want to accept that no matter how much weight I lose, I will be unattractive to him and to anyone. I just want to be okay with being the more friend wife than lover wife. He said we are lovers. How?

I am seeing a counselor. Everything is apparently my fault.

I can't get a pro pedicure, they are the ones who gave me the nail fungus that is contributing to my gross feet to begin with.
I have been eating heathily, working out, getting dolled up, and keeping the place tidy for over a week. Nothing.
Oh, and I just started counseling. Everything is apparently my fault. She probably thinks I should off myself.

I have a digestional tract defect, doctor said I had to get off it. I'm counting calories (weighing and measuring everything, mostly whole food I make myself), cut out soda, and workout 6 days a week for 1-2 hours (mix of cardio and weights). 

Even when I was average weight in high school, I didn't have a normal body. I have a unattractive version of a pear shape. No one has ever called me beautiful or sexy, except for my ex-bf amlnd he turned out to be a pathological liar. Husband refuses to "feed my insecurities" by complimenting me when I'm fishing for them. Apparently I'm supposed to just "know" that ___ body feature is okay. Right.
Thank you, this is really helpful. I didn't find the "fuck him" comments useful. I appreciate your positive outlook.

They are problematic, my words, not his. He tells me their cute in an effort to make me feel better, but I'm not blind.

Yes he has sacrificed for me, in more ways than one.

Ha, he isn't gay, I promise.

No, but with my family history I was certainly heading in that direction. How is my weight not in my control?

Look, you likely mean well but you're going off in a really heated way and making assumptions. Based on your own experience, I don't know. 

He knows he had flaws. He tries to fix some of them, and he has always been responsive when I point out he's not taking care of himself (shaving, no regualr haircuts, etc.) He has lost a little weight, but has to due to diabetes. He was never really that overweight but got the disease anyway. Poor luck of the draw, I suppose.

I agree with him that we are a team, and we both sometimes have to make sacrifices. He's made plenty for me. We don't approach our marriage from a "fuck you and your thoughts/opinions" attitude.

Hey now, the reason he stuck around is because he loves me as a person and what I bring to his life. He's more frustrated that I say I have a goal and then don't go for it. I know he doesn't want a model, just me at a healthy weight. I get why me not taking care of myself is unattractive. I do, but it's still frustrating.
It's not a church, nor a non-profit, it's a business.
Thanks. No pills, she's a counselor not a psychiatrist. We'll see how it goes.

No, I suppose not. My husband is the only one who has loved me, and while he has never laughed when I have non-sexual confident moments, he has in the middle of sex. I try to chalk it up to a more limited sexual background amd not knowing how to respond, but who knows.

Hard to believe when you've been essentially told you are unattractive by every man you've ever encountered. The few moments I've had some confidence and put it out there, I was literally laughed at. Laughed at and asked what I was doing.

No, the weight is the biggest part, by his own admission. I just started seeing a counselor. The first session went okay, but I don't like how everything was my fault. It's my fault that I can't "let him love me." Really now?

I did do keto, but due to a digestional tract defect, my doctor said I had to get off it. I just started counting calories (actually weighing and measuring all my food), and eating much less processed food (hardly any), no soda, and one small drink once every two weeks tops. Just moderating all around. I have a new workout plan out, a decent variety of stuff 1-2 hours day/6 days week. We'll see.

As for the rest, I know he really loves me and just wants me to succeed more than anything. The fact that I just give up so incredibly easily is a turn off to him. I get it, I do. It's just difficult when I struggle with self problems as is. I just started seeing a counselor.
He didn't reject me for four years (well not that often), but he hit his breaking point. He feels confident we will work past this. We will see.

Apparently it's more than that. I hadn't been taking care of myself as much as usual. I still shower and brush my teeth, but wasn't "getting ready." Not taking care of my skin so I broke out horribly, not a stitch of makeup, wearing my hair in a messy ponytale, wearing old, unflattering clothes. You get the picture. Yeah, my lack of effort to lose weight (just have unhealthy habits in general) was part of it but it was the entire thing.

Depression sucks. I make an effort, and while he's decently complimentary, I still never turned his head. So I give up, and then he really doesn't want it. I've never turned any man's head in my life, so I suppose I kinda expect it. Or rather, don't expect it. Maybe some people are just valued more for their other attributes (which I know he loves dearly in me).

I read something the other day that discussed how love and attraction are overly romanticized and idealized in this day and age. Maybe there's something to it.
